guitar.modelsText: 1959 Ford Belair-modified Esquire-style / vintage Fender Telecaster, Gibson J-45 acoustic
models: vintage Fender Telecaster, Gibson J-45 acoustic
guitar.evidence: Stapleton is known for playing a heavily modified/vintage-style Telecaster-esque electric guitar (often called his 'Esquire-ish' guitar) and a Gibson J-45 acoustic; documented in interviews and gear press but not universally iconic to casual listeners.
guitar.notes: Filled from unknown with medium confidence given decent documentation in guitar press.

tone.summary: A warm, compressed signal chain using a Fender-style amp and 2x12 cab, enhanced by light OD and room reverb for classic Americana sound.

rig.name: Chris Stapleton - Tennessee Whiskey - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Smooth dynamics and add sustain for a polished clean sound.
Provide light breakup and warmth without heavy crunch.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used to simulate the subtle grit of a Telecaster or vintage combo amp, avoiding modern rock tones.
The V-Wah or C-Wah would be too prominent and distracting.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the clean, warm tone of a Fender-style combo amp.

alternatives.reason: Similar sound, but US Deluxe is often better for the specified mid-push.

blocks.purpose: Match the specified smaller, vintage combo speaker cabinet.
Enhance the mid-range presence and warmth (mid push).
Add a short, natural room ambiance without sounding digital.
blocks.gap: The Room module is ideal for subtle, non-intrusive ambience required by the genre.

alternatives.reason: Can sound too artificial or bright.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism by swapping the default 2x12 IR for a vintage, smaller-sounding cab to better match the Americana/Fender combo aesthetic.

proposals.reason: Enhance vintage, smaller-cab character for Americana tone.
